newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia court dismisses election rigging petition.
newsitem.headline: Zambia court dismisses election rigging petition.

text.p: The Zambian Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed a petition filed against the country's electoral commission by opposition parties challenging the outcome of national elections last November.
The court also sentenced a Zambian journalist to three months in jail for claiming in a report that the court was bribed by the state to dismiss electoral petitions filed by four opposition parties.
The parties, including that of former president Kenneth Kaunda, are accusing President Frederick Chiluba and the electoral commission of trying to rig the election.

However, the court ruled on Tuesday that there was no reasonable case against the electoral commission. It also lifted an injuction restraining the commission from organising local government and parliamentary by-elections.
"The court has ruled that all orders against the electoral commission, including the injunction, fall away," Judge Ernest Sakala said.
He said reasons for the judgment would be released later.
Opposition parties alleged that the electoral commission had helped the ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy to rig the election.
They also alleged that President Chiluba, who won the elections with a landslide, lied about his parentage and nationality when he filed his electoral nomination papers.
Under a new constitution, presidential candidates must prove that they and their parents were born in Zambia.
The hearing on the petition against President Chiluba is scheduled to continue later on Tuesday.
Earlier, the court sentenced editor of special projects on the independent Post newspaper, Masautso Phiri, to three months imprisonment for contempt.
Phiri alleged in an article in December that the state had offered the seven Supreme Court judges a total of 14 billion kwacha ($10.6 million) to dismiss the electoral petitions.
On Monday, Phiri told the court that he did not mean to question their integrity and asked for their forgiveness.
